topic: Cómo los bancos crean dinero prestando tus depósitos
title: Your Bank Barely Has Your Money
title_alternatives: Where Your Bank Deposit Actually Goes
Banks Lend Money They Don't Hold
format_rationale: Un solo mecanismo sorprendente (préstamo de depósitos) que se entiende con hook → giro → payoff en menos de 60 s.

idea.angle: El dinero que crees guardado está prestado y multiplicado
idea.promise: Entender en 1 minuto dónde está realmente tu dinero
idea.curiosity_gap: ¿Si el banco no tiene mi dinero, dónde está?
idea.target_viewer: Adulto joven con cuenta bancaria y poca educación financiera
idea.rpm_reason: Banca, ahorro y seguros de depósito atraen anunciantes financieros de alto CPM

structure.purpose: Afirmación chocante que contradice lo que el espectador cree
Mecanismo de creación de dinero en 3 golpes con mini-sorpresas
El riesgo (bank run) y la red de protección
Cierre que repite la frase del hook para el loop

script.full_text: Your bank barely has your money. Wait, I deposited my savings there last week! Here is the trick nobody explains at school. Deposit a dollar, and the bank doesn't lock it away. It keeps a small slice and lends out the rest. And I happily borrow it to buy another building. The builder deposits that money in another bank. So that bank lends it out again? Like a copy machine? Exactly. One dollar becomes many dollars on paper. Economists call this money creation through lending. It fuels growth, houses and businesses when things go well. But what if everybody wants their money back at once? Then the bank simply doesn't have it. A bank run. Which is why I never keep everything in one place. Today deposit insurance and central banks stand behind the system. It's out working, multiplying across the economy. It is out working, moving, multiplying across the whole economy. A promise. Because your bank barely has your money. A promise. Because your bank has almost none of your money.
